name: Ataxia-oculomotor apraxia type 1

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Ataxia-oculomotor apraxia type 1

criteria.description: Progressive cerebellar ataxia with gait disturbance
Presence of oculomotor apraxia characterized by impaired voluntary horizontal eye movements
Sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy confirmed by nerve conduction studies
Biallelic pathogenic variants in the APTX gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive cerebellar ataxia, oculomotor apraxia, peripheral neuropathy, and biallelic pathogenic variants in APTX gene
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Elevated alpha-fetoprotein is supportive but not mandatory; diagnosis confirmed by genetic testing.

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated creatine kinase
other: Nerve conduction studies showing sensorimotor axonal neuropathy

distinguishingFeatures: Later onset (usually adolescence or early adulthood)
Elevated alpha-fetoprotein but with ATM gene mutations

redFlags: Rapidly progressive ataxia with early oculomotor apraxia
Early onset peripheral neuropathy with cerebellar signs
Elevated alpha-fetoprotein in a child with neurological symptoms
references: Anheim M, Tranchant C. Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 1. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2008;3:15.
Moreira MC, Barbot C, Tachi N, et al. The gene mutated in ataxia-oculomotor apraxia 1 encodes a new HIT/Zn-finger protein. Nat Genet. 2001;29(2):184-188.
Hirano M, Nishio SY, Tsuji S. Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 1: clinical and molecular features. Neurol Clin. 2012;30(4):1043-1052.
